issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() (returning a String), but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and all Rideable implementations (Pig, Seal) use a String parameter. This parameter mismatch makes it unclear which signature students should implement and prevents code in the template (Main.java) that calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments from compiling against the solution-style interfaces.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/template by removing the parameter: declare String messageOnRide() in Rideable and update Pig/Seal to implement the no-arg version (returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"), or (B) update the problem statement and template examples to require messageOnRide(String equipment) and reflect the equipment parameter everywhere (including the Main.java calls). Prefer option A to match the current exercise description.

issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method is specified and used as a no-argument method in the problem statement and the template (students are shown calling r.messageOnRide()), but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implements it with a parameter. This changes the method signature for the same conceptual operation (riding an animal) across artifacts, creating a mismatch students must resolve and causing the example/template usage to be inconsistent with the solution API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to define messageOnRide() with no parameters and update implementing classes (Pig, Seal) to return the text "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (removing the equipment parameter), or (B) update the problem statement and template examples to require and pass a String equipment parameter to messageOnRide(String equipment). Prefer option (A) to match the current problem description and template usage.
